title: Ezra 7:12 (the king’s greeting) — “perfect peace” against “let the word and the answer be completed”
summary: Ezra 7:12 in the KJV greets Ezra with “perfect peace, and at such a time”. The old Greek translation asks that the word and answer be completed. The source language of this verse is Aramaic.
text: KJV Ezra 7:12: “Artaxerxes, king of kings, unto Ezra the priest, a scribe of the law of the God of heaven, perfect peace, and at such a time.” Aramaic text Ezra 7:12: אַ֨רְתַּחְשַׁ֔סְתְּא מֶ֖לֶךְ מַלְכַיָּ֑א לְעֶזְרָ֣א כָ֠הֲנָא סָפַ֨ר דָּתָ֜א דִּֽי־אֱלָ֧הּ שְׁמַיָּ֛א גְּמִ֖יר וּכְעֶֽנֶת׃ [Aramaic rendering: complete, and now.] Old Greek translation Ezra 7:12: Ἀρθασασθὰ βασιλεὺς βασιλέων Ἔσδρᾳ γραμματεῖ νόμου Κυρίου τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ· τετελέσθω λόγος καὶ ἡ ἀπόκρισις. [Greek rendering: let a word and the answer be completed.]
reasoning: The KJV presents a greeting of peace, while this Greek wording presents a request for completion. The Aramaic text does not include a word for peace.
scope: This finding concerns the greeting/completion wording at Ezra 7:12 only. The difficult Aramaic phrase does not establish a KJV translation error here. This record does not prove the meaning of a Persian official formula. The cited Greek edition groups Ezra and Nehemiah under Esdras. title: Ezra 7:26 (the king’s penalties) — “banishment” against “chastisement”
summary: Ezra 7:26 in the KJV lists death, banishment, loss of goods and imprisonment. The old Greek translation uses chastisement, or corrective punishment, as its second item. Both lists have four items.
text: KJV Ezra 7:26: “And whosoever will not do the law of thy God, and the law of the king, let judgment be executed speedily upon him, whether it be unto death, or to banishment, or to confiscation of goods, or to imprisonment.” Aramaic text Ezra 7:26: וְכָל־דִּי־לָא֩ לֶהֱוֵ֨א עָבֵ֜ד דָּתָ֣א דִֽי־אֱלָהָ֗ךְ וְדָתָא֙ דִּ֣י מַלְכָּ֔א אָסְפַּ֕רְנָא דִּינָ֕ה לֶהֱוֵ֥א מִתְעֲבֵ֖ד מִנֵּ֑הּ הֵ֤ן לְמֹות֙ הֵ֣ן [לִשְׁרֹשׁוּ כ] (לִשְׁרֹשִׁ֔י ק) הֵן־לַעֲנָ֥שׁ נִכְסִ֖ין וְלֶאֱסוּרִֽין׃  פ [Aramaic: the text marks separate forms to write and to read; their meaning is not settled here.] Old Greek translation Ezra 7:26: Καὶ πὰς ὃς ἂν μὴ ᾖ ποιῶν νόμον τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ νόμον τοῦ βασιλέως ἑτοίμως, τὸ κρίμα ἔσται γινόμενον ἐξ αὐτοῦ, ἐάν τε εἰς θάνατον, ἐάν τε εἰς παιδείαν, ἐάν τε εἰς ζημίαν τοῦ βίου. ἐάν τε εἰς παράδοσιν. [Greek rendering: to death, to chastisement, to loss of property, to delivery.]
reasoning: The comparison is banishment versus corrective punishment in the second position. The Greek does not add an extra penalty.
scope: The finding concerns only the second penalty at Ezra 7:26. The fourth items are outside this comparison. title: Ezra 9:7 (Ezra’s prayer) — “our priests” against “our children”
summary: At Ezra 9:7, the KJV and Hebrew text name “our kings, and our priests” among those handed over. The old Greek translation instead names our sons.
text: KJV Ezra 9:7: “Since the days of our fathers have we been in a great trespass unto this day; and for our iniquities have we, our kings, and our priests, been delivered into the hand of the kings of the lands, to the sword, to captivity, and to a spoil, and to confusion of face, as it is this day.” Hebrew text Ezra 9:7: מִימֵ֣י אֲבֹתֵ֗ינוּ אֲנַ֙חְנוּ֙ בְּאַשְׁמָ֣ה גְדֹלָ֔ה עַ֖ד הַיֹּ֣ום הַזֶּ֑ה וּבַעֲוֹנֹתֵ֡ינוּ נִתַּ֡נּוּ אֲנַחְנוּ֩ מְלָכֵ֨ינוּ כֹהֲנֵ֜ינוּ בְּיַ֣ד ׀ מַלְכֵ֣י הָאֲרָצֹ֗ות בַּחֶ֜רֶב בַּשְּׁבִ֧י וּבַבִּזָּ֛ה וּבְבֹ֥שֶׁת פָּנִ֖ים כְּהַיֹּ֥ום הַזֶּֽה׃ [Hebrew rendering: our priests.] Old Greek translation Ezra 9:7: Ἀπὸ ἡμερῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν ἐσμὲν ἐν πλημμελείᾳ μεγάλῃ ἕως τῆς ἡμέρας ταύτης· καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἀνομίαις ἡμῶν παρεδόθημεν ἡμεῖς καὶ οἱ βασιλεῖς ἡμῶν καὶ οἱ υἱοὶ ἡμῶν ἐν χειρὶ βασιλέων τῶν ἐθνῶν ἐν ῥομφαίᾳ, καὶ ἐν αἰχμαλωσίᾳ, καιὶ ἐν διαρπαγῇ, καὶ ἐν αἰσχύνῃ προσώπου ἡμῶν, ὡς ἡ ἡμέρα αὕτη. title: Ezra 9:13–14 — “punished us less than our iniquities deserve” and a question of anger, against “there is none such as our God” and a plea
summary: At Ezra 9:13, the KJV says God has “punished us less than our iniquities deserve”. Verse 14 asks whether God would be angry if they sinned again. The old Greek translation describes God as unequalled, lightening their wrongs, then pleads that God not be angry.
text: KJV Ezra 9:13–14: “And after all that is come upon us for our evil deeds, and for our great trespass, seeing that thou our God hast punished us less than our iniquities deserve, and hast given us such deliverance as this; Should we again break thy commandments, and join in affinity with the people of these abominations? wouldest not thou be angry with us till thou hadst consumed us, so that there should be no remnant nor escaping?” Hebrew text Ezra 9:13–14: וְאַֽחֲרֵי֙ כָּל־הַבָּ֣א עָלֵ֔ינוּ בְּמַעֲשֵׂ֙ינוּ֙ הָרָעִ֔ים וּבְאַשְׁמָתֵ֖נוּ הַגְּדֹלָ֑ה כִּ֣י ׀ אַתָּ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ חָשַׂ֤כְתָּֽ לְמַ֙טָּה֙ מֵֽעֲוֹנֵ֔נוּ וְנָתַ֥תָּה לָּ֛נוּ פְּלֵיטָ֖ה כָּזֹֽאת׃ הֲנָשׁוּב֙ לְהָפֵ֣ר מִצְוֹתֶ֔יךָ וּ֨לְהִתְחַתֵּ֔ן בְּעַמֵּ֥י הַתֹּעֵבֹ֖ות הָאֵ֑לֶּה הֲלֹ֤וא תֶֽאֱנַף־בָּ֙נוּ֙ עַד־כַּלֵּ֔ה לְאֵ֥ין שְׁאֵרִ֖ית וּפְלֵיטָֽה׃  פ [Hebrew rendering: 13, you held back beneath our wrongs; 14, will you not be angry with us.] Old Greek translation Ezra 9:13–14: Καὶ μετὰ πᾶν τὸ ἐρχόμενον ἐφʼ ἡμᾶς ἐν ποιήμασιν ἡμῶν τοῖς πονηροῖς καὶ ἐν πλημμελείᾳ ἡμῶν τῇ μεγάλῃ, ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν ὡς ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν, ὅτι ἐκούφισας ἡμῶν τὰς ἀνομίας, καὶ ἔδωκας ἡμῖν σωτηρίαν· Ὅτι ἐπεστρέψαμεν διασκεδάσαι ἐντολάς σου, καὶ ἐπιγαμβρεῦσαι τοῖς λαοῖς τῶν γαιῶν· μὴ παροξυνθῇς ἐν ἡμῖν ἕως συντελείας, τοῦ μὴ εἶναι ἐγκατάλειμμα καὶ διασωζόμενον. [Greek rendering: 13, there is none like our God, for you lightened our wrongs. 14, do not be angry with us.]
reasoning: The KJV joins a statement about lighter punishment with a question about anger. This Greek edition includes the fuller statement about God and frames the anger clause as a plea.
scope: The finding concerns Ezra 9:13 and Ezra 9:14 only. The question and plea may reflect choices in translation. This record does not decide Ezra's intended meaning or claim a KJV error. title: Nehemiah 5:5 (the complaint of the poor) — “other men have our lands” against “our fields belong to the honourable”
summary: At Nehemiah 5:5, the KJV says “other men have our lands and vineyards”. The Hebrew text names others. The old Greek translation calls them honourable people.
text: KJV Nehemiah 5:5: “Yet now our flesh is as the flesh of our brethren, our children as their children: and, lo, we bring into bondage our sons and our daughters to be servants, and some of our daughters are brought unto bondage already: neither is it in our power to redeem them; for other men have our lands and vineyards.” Hebrew text Nehemiah 5:5: וְעַתָּ֗ה כִּבְשַׂ֤ר אַחֵ֙ינוּ֙ בְּשָׂרֵ֔נוּ כִּבְנֵיהֶ֖ם בָּנֵ֑ינוּ וְהִנֵּ֣ה אֲנַ֣חְנוּ כֹ֠בְשִׁים אֶת־בָּנֵ֨ינוּ וְאֶת־בְּנֹתֵ֜ינוּ לַעֲבָדִ֗ים וְיֵ֨שׁ מִבְּנֹתֵ֤ינוּ נִכְבָּשֹׁות֙ וְאֵ֣ין לְאֵ֣ל יָדֵ֔נוּ וּשְׂדֹתֵ֥ינוּ וּכְרָמֵ֖ינוּ לַאֲחֵרִֽים׃ [Hebrew rendering: to others.] Old Greek translation Nehemiah 5:5: Καὶ νῦν ὡς σὰρξ ἀδελφῶν ἡμῶν, σὰρξ ἡμῶν· ὡς υἱοὶ αὐτῶν, υἱοὶ ἡμῶν· καὶ ἰδοὺ ἡμεῖς καταδυναστεύομεν τοὺς υἱοὺς ἡμῶν καὶ τὰς θυγατέρας ἡμῶν εἰς δούλους, καὶ εἰσὶν ἀπὸ θυγατέρων ἡμῶν καταδυναστευόμεναι, καὶ οὐκ ἔστι δύναμις χειρῶν ἡμῶν, καὶ ἀγροὶ ἡμῶν καὶ ἀμπελῶνες ἡμῶν τοῖς ἐντίμοις. [Greek rendering: to the honoured, or honourable.]
reasoning: Others leaves the group unnamed; honourable describes its standing. That wording does not identify particular officials or explain their motives.

title: Nehemiah 5:14, 18 — “the bread of the governor” against “provision extorted” and “the bread of extortion”
summary: At Nehemiah 5:14 and 5:18, the KJV says Nehemiah did not take “the bread of the governor”. The Hebrew text names the governor too. The old Greek translation uses force at 5:14 and bread of force or extortion at 5:18.
text: KJV Nehemiah 5:14, 18: “Moreover from the time that I was appointed to be their governor in the land of Judah, from the twentieth year even unto the two and thirtieth year of Artaxerxes the king, that is, twelve years, I and my brethren have not eaten the bread of the governor. Now that which was prepared for me daily was one ox and six choice sheep; also fowls were prepared for me, and once in ten days store of all sorts of wine: yet for all this required not I the bread of the governor, because the bondage was heavy upon this people.” Hebrew text Nehemiah 5:14, 18: גַּ֞ם מִיֹּ֣ום ׀ אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֣ה אֹתִ֗י לִהְיֹ֣ות פֶּחָם֮ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ יְהוּדָה֒ מִשְּׁנַ֣ת עֶשְׂרִ֗ים וְ֠עַד שְׁנַ֨ת שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וּשְׁתַּ֙יִם֙ לְאַרְתַּחְשַׁ֣סְתְּא הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ שָׁנִ֖ים שְׁתֵּ֣ים עֶשְׂרֵ֑ה אֲנִ֣י וְאַחַ֔י לֶ֥חֶם הַפֶּ֖חָה לֹ֥א אָכַֽלְתִּי׃ וַאֲשֶׁר֩ הָיָ֨ה נַעֲשֶׂ֜ה לְיֹ֣ום אֶחָ֗ד שֹׁ֣ור אֶחָ֞ד צֹ֠אן שֵׁשׁ־בְּרֻרֹ֤ות וְצִפֳּרִים֙ נַֽעֲשׂוּ־לִ֔י וּבֵ֨ין עֲשֶׂ֧רֶת יָמִ֛ים בְּכָל־יַ֖יִן לְהַרְבֵּ֑ה וְעִם־זֶ֗ה לֶ֤חֶם הַפֶּחָה֙ לֹ֣א בִקַּ֔שְׁתִּי כִּֽי־כָֽבְדָ֥ה הָעֲבֹדָ֖ה עַל־הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּֽה׃ [Hebrew rendering: bread of the governor, in 14 and 18.] Old Greek translation Nehemiah 5:14, 18: Ἀπὸ ἡμέρας ἧς ἐνετείλατό μοι εἶναι εἰς ἄρχοντα αὐτῶν ἐν γῇ Ἰούδα, ἀπὸ ἔτους εἰκοστοῦ καὶ ἕως ἔτους τριακοστοῦ καὶ δευτέρου τῷ Ἀρθασασθὰ ἔτη δώδεκα, ἐγὼ καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοί μου βίαν αὐτῶν οὐκ ἔφαγον. Καὶ ἦν γινόμενον εἰς ἡμέραν μίαν μόσχος εἷς, καὶ πρόβατα ἓξ ἐκλεκτὰ καὶ χίμαρος ἐγίνοντό μοι· καὶ ἀναμέσον δέκα ἡμερῶν ἐν πᾶσιν οἶνος τῷ πλήθει· καὶ σὺν τούτοις ἄρτους τῆς βίας οὐκ ἐζήτησα, ὅτι βαρεῖα ἡ δουλεία ἐπὶ τὸν λαὸν τοῦτον. [Greek rendering: 14, I did not eat their force. 18, I did not seek the bread of force.]
reasoning: The KJV names the governor's office and its allowance. The Greek wording describes force or harsh demands. Its verse 5:15 gives nearby context about earlier rulers burdening the people.

title: Nehemiah 5:18 (Nehemiah’s table) — “fowls” against “a goat”
summary: At Nehemiah 5:18, the KJV lists one ox, six choice sheep and fowls for the daily meal. The Hebrew text has birds. The old Greek translation has a goat in their place.
text: KJV Nehemiah 5:18: “Now that which was prepared for me daily was one ox and six choice sheep; also fowls were prepared for me, and once in ten days store of all sorts of wine: yet for all this required not I the bread of the governor, because the bondage was heavy upon this people.” Hebrew text Nehemiah 5:18: וַאֲשֶׁר֩ הָיָ֨ה נַעֲשֶׂ֜ה לְיֹ֣ום אֶחָ֗ד שֹׁ֣ור אֶחָ֞ד צֹ֠אן שֵׁשׁ־בְּרֻרֹ֤ות וְצִפֳּרִים֙ נַֽעֲשׂוּ־לִ֔י וּבֵ֨ין עֲשֶׂ֧רֶת יָמִ֛ים בְּכָל־יַ֖יִן לְהַרְבֵּ֑ה וְעִם־זֶ֗ה לֶ֤חֶם הַפֶּחָה֙ לֹ֣א בִקַּ֔שְׁתִּי כִּֽי־כָֽבְדָ֥ה הָעֲבֹדָ֖ה עַל־הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּֽה׃ [Hebrew rendering: one bull, six choice sheep, and birds.] Old Greek translation Nehemiah 5:18: Καὶ ἦν γινόμενον εἰς ἡμέραν μίαν μόσχος εἷς, καὶ πρόβατα ἓξ ἐκλεκτὰ καὶ χίμαρος ἐγίνοντό μοι· καὶ ἀναμέσον δέκα ἡμερῶν ἐν πᾶσιν οἶνος τῷ πλήθει· καὶ σὺν τούτοις ἄρτους τῆς βίας οὐκ ἐζήτησα, ὅτι βαρεῖα ἡ δουλεία ἐπὶ τὸν λαὸν τοῦτον. [Greek rendering: one calf, six choice sheep and a kid-goat.]
reasoning: The finding is birds versus a goat. The separate ox/calf wording is outside this comparison.

title: Nehemiah 13:16 — “men of Tyre” against “they sat in it”
summary: At Nehemiah 13:16, the KJV and Hebrew text identify fish sellers as people from Tyre. The old Greek translation describes people bringing fish without naming Tyre.
text: KJV Nehemiah 13:16: “There dwelt men of Tyre also therein, which brought fish, and all manner of ware, and sold on the sabbath unto the children of Judah, and in Jerusalem.” Hebrew text Nehemiah 13:16: וְהַצֹּרִים֙ יָ֣שְׁבוּ בָ֔הּ מְבִיאִ֥ים דָּ֖אג וְכָל־מֶ֑כֶר וּמֹכְרִ֧ים בַּשַּׁבָּ֛ת לִבְנֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה וּבִירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ [Hebrew rendering: and the Tyrians dwelt in it.] Old Greek translation Nehemiah 13:16: Καὶ ἐκάθισαν ἐν αὐτῇ φέροντες ἰχθὺν, καὶ πᾶσαν πρᾶσιν πωλοῦντες τῷ σαββάτῳ τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰούδα καὶ ἐν Ἱερουσαλήμ. [Greek rendering: and they dwelt in it, with no name for Tyre or its people.]
reasoning: The compared Greek wording leaves out the place name. It does not deny that the sellers came from Tyre.

title: Nehemiah 13:25 — “or for yourselves” is not in the Greek
summary: At Nehemiah 13:25, the KJV forbids taking foreign daughters for the men's sons “or for yourselves”. The Hebrew text includes that ending. The old Greek translation ends with the sons.
text: KJV Nehemiah 13:25: “And I contended with them, and cursed them, and smote certain of them, and plucked off their hair, and made them swear by God, saying, Ye shall not give your daughters unto their sons, nor take their daughters unto your sons, or for yourselves.” Hebrew text Nehemiah 13:25: וָאָרִ֤יב עִמָּם֙ וָאֲקַֽלְלֵ֔ם וָאַכֶּ֥ה מֵהֶ֛ם אֲנָשִׁ֖ים וָֽאֶמְרְטֵ֑ם וָאַשְׁבִּיעֵ֣ם בֵּֽאלֹהִ֗ים אִם־תִּתְּנ֤וּ בְנֹֽתֵיכֶם֙ לִבְנֵיהֶ֔ם וְאִם־תִּשְׂאוּ֙ מִבְּנֹ֣תֵיהֶ֔ם לִבְנֵיכֶ֖ם וְלָכֶֽם׃ [Hebrew rendering: for your sons or for you.] Old Greek translation Nehemiah 13:25: Καὶ ἐμαχεσάμην μετʼ αὐτῶν, καὶ καταρασάμην αὐτούς· καὶ ἐπάταξα ἐν αὐτοῖς ἄνδρας, καὶ ἐμαδάρωσα αὐτοὺς, καὶ ὤρκισα αὐτοὺς ἐν τῷ Θεῷ, ἐὰν δῶτε τὰς θυγατέρας ὑμῶν τοῖς υἱοῖς αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐὰν λάβητε ἀπὸ τῶν θυγατέρων αὐτῶν τοῖς υἱοῖς ὑμῶν. [Greek rendering: if you take of their daughters for your sons. No further phrase follows.]
reasoning: The printed Greek lacks the closing phrase naming the men themselves. Its absence does not establish that the rule exempts them.
